newsitem.title: FRANCE: Arthuis pledges further cuts in payroll charges.
newsitem.headline: Arthuis pledges further cuts in payroll charges.

text.p: The French government plans to make new reductions in payroll charges as soon as economic growth allows, French Finance Minister Jean Arthuis said on Tuesday.

"As soon as our determined and coherent policy in favour of growth returns enough room for manoeuvre, we will begin a resolute drive to make new reductions in payroll charges because these are what weigh on our competitiveness and our employment," he told parliament.
Arthuis, speaking in a debate on the 1997 budget, said that tackling unemployment, which has risen to a record 12.6 percent, remained one of the government's top priorities.
He noted however that the 1997 budget would "refocus" government policies which aim to reduce payroll charges to lower the cost of labour and boost employment.
The government plans to cut next year a number of unsuccessful job-creation schemes, many of which revolved around subsidising payroll charges, to reduce spending.
The schemes will be refocused to help those most in need, like the long-term unemployed.
Many private economists blame France's high unemployment rate on heavy payroll charges, used to finance the generous welfare system, and labour force inflexibility.
They argue that without structural reforms, even strong economic growth cannot bring the unemployment rate below a level of around eight percent.
